pagina.entradilla: A white town between two hills, at the foot of a castle of the Order of Santiago. It was the capital of the Encomienda Mayor de León of the Order of Santiago, and every September the Plaza de España is closed off for the Capeas.
pagina.descripcion: History, heritage, festivals and food of Segura de León (Badajoz, Spain).

historia: There was a Roman villa at the site known as El Torreón, near the Cristo de la Reja. The Order of Santiago conquered these lands in 1248, and in 1274 Master Pelay Pérez Correa granted the town a fuero (charter of rights), which thereby separated it from Montemolín.

Segura was the capital of the Encomienda Mayor de León (the main commandery of the Order of Santiago) and the seat of the Vicaría de Tudía until the 19th century; hence the cross of Santiago and the lion on its coat of arms. It was also the head of a judicial district from 1274 to 1834.

In the 14th century the Order built the castle, and Alonso de Cárdenas, the last master, made it his palace. The town had a Jewish quarter until 1492, and in 1483 the financier and theologian Isaac Abravanel lived there.

From its pine woods came beams, planks, chairs and pine nuts that the people of Segura sold across the south of Extremadura. In 1973 the Diputación (provincial council) bought the castle for a million pesetas and handed it over to the Town Council, which has restored it and now opens it to visitors.

El castillo.texto: A castle of the Order of Santiago, from the 14th century, with the keep (torre del Homenaje) and its 24 battlements. It can be visited with an audio guide.
El castillo.alt: The battlemented castle above the whitewashed houses of the town

Iglesia de la Asunción.texto: A Site of Cultural Interest (Bien de Interés Cultural) since 2009. It holds a canvas by Valdés Leal and a Baroque organ of 1782.
Iglesia de la Asunción.alt: The parish church among the rooftops, with the hill behind

Convento de San Benito.texto: Franciscan, from 1477-1480, with a Mudéjar cloister and the Cristo de la Reja, patron of the Capeas.
Convento de San Benito.alt: The whitewashed convent of San Benito at the end of a dirt track

Casa Consistorial.texto: From 1555, with arcades and the imperial coat of arms of Charles V. It presides over the Plaza de España.
Casa Consistorial.alt: The white façade of the Town Hall with arcades and a clock

Ermita de los Remedios.texto: With a porch of 1833 and a Baroque altarpiece. The cemetery is next to it.
Ermita de los Remedios.alt: The white chapel among the dehesa and the meadows

Calles y tejados.texto: The whitewashed houses, seen from the castle's wall-walk (paseo de ronda).
Calles y tejados.alt: White streets and red roofs with the tower of the parish church

Las Capeas.texto: Every September the Plaza de España is closed off with wooden stands (tablaos) to fight the cows lent by the cattle breeders.
Las Capeas.alt: Riders and cattle entering the square, closed off with wooden stands

placa.titulo: The cartouche of the Jewish quarter
placa.pie: Cartouche from a house in the old aljama (Jewish quarter)
placa.texto: «In the Lord I trust». The Jewish quarter took in Calle Castillo, Calle Portugalejo, Calle Santa Cruz and Calle Mesones; the synagogue, now gone, stood in Calle Castillo.

Castillo santiaguista.nombre: Castillo santiaguista (castle of the Order of Santiago)
Castillo santiaguista.detalle: 14th century. The Miramontes and Alcaides towers, the keep with 24 battlements, a chapel, a dungeon and two cisterns.

Iglesia parroquial de Nuestra Señora de.nombre: Parish church of Our Lady of the Assumption
Iglesia parroquial de Nuestra Señora de.detalle: Site of Cultural Interest (BIC, 2009). An inscription of 1299, the Hernán Mejías chapel, 13 altarpieces, Valdés Leal's «Martirio de San Bartolomé» (Martyrdom of Saint Bartholomew) and the organ by Tomás Risueño (1782).

Convento de San Benito y Cristo de la Re.nombre: Convent of San Benito and Cristo de la Reja
Convento de San Benito y Cristo de la Re.detalle: Franciscan, from 1477-1480. A double Mudéjar cloister with 17th-century tempera paintings and the carving of the Christ, from the early 16th century, attributed to Pedro Millán.

Casa Consistorial.detalle: From 1555, rebuilt in 1967. It keeps the arches and the imperial coat of arms of Charles V.

Casa del Gobernador.detalle: Home of the governor or chief magistrate (alcalde mayor) from the 16th century to 1833, with a granite doorway and grotesque decoration.

Convento de la Limpia Concepción (iglesi.nombre: Convent of the Limpia Concepción (Fátima church)
Convento de la Limpia Concepción (iglesi.detalle: Founded around 1571-1573 by García de Merlo and Beatriz Núñez for Conceptionist nuns, who stayed there until 1870.

Ermita de los Remedios y cementerio.nombre: Chapel of Los Remedios and cemetery
Ermita de los Remedios y cementerio.detalle: A porch of 1833 and a Baroque altarpiece of the 18th century. The cemetery dates from 1829.

Ermita de las Angustias.detalle: From the early 16th century, with an Isabelline doorway.

Ermita de San Roque.detalle: From the old hospital of San Roque (17th century), with the image of the patron saint.

Aljama o judería.detalle: Between Calle Castillo, Calle Portugalejo, Calle Santa Cruz and Calle Mesones, with the cartouche of 1554.

Plazas y arquerías.detalle: The Plaza de España, the Plaza de la Iglesia and the Plaza de Don Carmelo, and the arcades of Calle San Roque.

Monumento al Sagrado Corazón.detalle: Unveiled in 1930 on the Cerro de la Piedra Gorda. It is a viewpoint.

Tesoro de la Martela.detalle: Gold jewellery of the 4th century BC found in 1984. It is in the Museo Arqueológico de Badajoz (Archaeological Museum of Badajoz).

Molinos de aceite y Arcos de la Alcantar.nombre: Oil mills and the Arcos de la Alcantarilla
Molinos de aceite y Arcos de la Alcantar.detalle: Beam-press towers in Calle Sánchez Miranda and Calle Enfermería, and the arches of the bridge over the Pasay stream (arroyo del Pasay).

Siete Fuentes.detalle: Santa María, the Caño, the Bejarana, the Pilar Chico, the Pilar Viejo, the Alcantarilla and the Carriona.

Sierra y castillo de Gigonza.detalle: At 738 m, with the remains of a Muslim castle of the 10th century.

Cañada Real Soriana y Charco Hondo.nombre: Cañada Real Soriana and Charco Hondo
Cañada Real Soriana y Charco Hondo.detalle: The drove road along which the flocks of the Mesta came down.

Candelaria y San Blas.nombre: Candelaria and San Blas (Candlemas and Saint Blaise)

Semana Santa.cuando: With the Amarrao, the madrugá and the Pregón de Pilatos

Virgen de los Remedios.cuando: The Monday of the week after Easter

San Isidro.cuando: The weekend after 15 May, with casetas (booths) in the Llano del Convento

Feria Gastronómica «Segura, para comérse.nombre: Food Fair «Segura, para comérsela» (Segura, good enough to eat)

San Roque, patrón, y la Asunción.nombre: San Roque (patron saint) and the Asunción (Assumption)
San Roque, patrón, y la Asunción.cuando: 15 and 16 August, with the Ramo and the merengues (meringues)

Las Capeas, en honor al Cristo de la Rej.nombre: Las Capeas, in honour of the Cristo de la Reja
Las Capeas, en honor al Cristo de la Rej.cuando: Mid-September; the 14th is the day of the Cristo

San Francisco.cuando: Around 4 October, in the Llano del Convento

platos: Tostadas con zurrapa o de caldillo (toast with zurrapa or with caldillo)
Ancas de rana rebozadas (battered frogs' legs)
Mushrooms: níscalos (saffron milk caps), boletos (boletes) and gurumelos
Game: partridge, rabbit and hare with rice
Sopas de ajo y de tomate (garlic and tomato soups)
Jamón ibérico de bellota (acorn-fed Iberian ham)

Alonso de Cárdenas.texto: The last master of the Order of Santiago. Comendador mayor (senior commander) from 1450, he made the castle his palace.

Leonor de Luna.texto: Wife of Alonso de Cárdenas and co-founder of the convent of San Benito.

Isaac Abravanel.texto: A financier and theologian who had fled from Portugal. He lived in Segura's Jewish quarter for nine months, from 1 June 1483.

Diego Mexías.texto: A captain in the conquest of Peru. His bequest paid for the Mexía chapel in the parish church.

Álvaro Martín.texto: An indiano (a man who made his fortune in the Americas) in Panama. He gave 1,600 ducats to the convent of San Benito, where his chapel is.

Beatriz Núñez.texto: Together with her husband, García de Merlo, she founded the convent of the Limpia Concepción.

Ildefonso Serrano.texto: «The Sage of Extremadura» (El Sabio de Extremadura). He founded a school, the magazine Lumen, a printing press, the agricultural union and the Caja Rural (rural savings bank).

José Pérez Jiménez.texto: A painter. He taught in Oviedo from 1914.

Guillermo Silveira.texto: A painter and sculptor. Gold medal of the 4th Extremaduran Biennial (1970).

Ruta Verde.resumen: 15 km, low difficulty. The Polígono, Juanadame, Charco Hondo, Los Molinillos and the swimming pool.

Ruta Roja.resumen: 12 km, low difficulty. El Tropezón, El Torreón, the Cristo de la Reja, Las Amarillas, La Contiña, Los Majadales and the Pilar Viejo.

Ruta Negra.resumen: 18 km, medium difficulty. Grano de Oro, Cuesta Casillas, the Cañada Real and the Fuente del Caño.

Ruta Azul.resumen: 21 km, low difficulty. Fuente de Santa María, El Sejo, La Orden, El Morito and Juanadame.

Ruta de las Siete Fuentes.resumen: Past the fountains that supplied the town with water, from Santa María to the Carriona.

Camino de Santiago.resumen: A stage of the Camino del Sur from Huelva: Fuentes de León, Segura de León and Valencia del Ventoso.
